quote: I'm moving I'm military, so I'm moving to Virginia... I don't close on my house till Friday.
stewart_read: The customer discloses a stressful life transition — active military relocation, a home purchase not yet closed, family moving separately in June — in his very first substantive answer. This isn't a listed trigger category in the schema (which covers loss, financial hardship, health, family caregiving) but it's the same structural signal: a life-transition disclosure that briefly opens trust. The rep skips past it entirely into the qualification script.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have judged this as background color rather than a moment requiring acknowledgment, which is a defensible read since the customer's tone stayed even rather than distressed.
coaching_implication: This is a light-touch coaching note, not a hard miss: a single line acknowledging the move ('that's a lot going on with the move and the closing') would have cost nothing and built rapport before diving into address verification. Worth flagging to the rep as a habit to build, not a failure to correct.

quote: We can definitely still show your design. Again, that's just to make it a little bit more accurate, but we can still take a look at it based off, like, the square footage and everything like that.
stewart_read: The customer explicitly says he has no idea what utility costs are in Virginia but has read that electricity there 'has skyrocketed.' This is a live curiosity hook — the customer is already primed to want to know the number — and the rep pivots straight to square footage as a proxy without ever reflecting the 'skyrocketed cost' idea back to him.
alternative_hypothesis: Since the customer has no bill and hasn't moved in, there may genuinely be no bill to anchor on this call, making the pivot to square footage a reasonable substitute data point.
coaching_implication: Even without a bill, the rep could have verbally flagged the specialist call as the moment he'll get a real answer to the 'skyrocketed costs' question he raised, converting the uncertainty into forward pull rather than letting it drop.

quote: is it an opportunity for me to, you know, invest in solar since we're gonna be there for a couple of years and, you know, hopefully, save some money?
stewart_read: The customer is asking, unprompted, whether solar makes sense given his expected tenure — a self-qualifying question that signals real intent beyond idle browsing. This is Stewart's own read, not something the schema currently documents (customer_demographics and what_good_looks_like sections covering tenure signals are marked TBD in the schema); the rep does not acknowledge or reinforce this framing anywhere later in the call.
coaching_implication: Reps should be coached to catch and echo self-qualifying questions like this — a quick 'exactly, and that's the kind of math the specialist will run for you' would have validated the customer's own reasoning and kept him bought in through the reschedule negotiation that follows.

quote: Do you know if that's like an asphalt shingle roof? It looks like it is. It is. It is.
stewart_read: Rep runs the roof-type verify item efficiently, confirming visually before asking, which speeds the section without feeling like an interrogation.
coaching_implication: This is a positive procedural note — worth naming as a repeatable habit (visual pre-check before asking) rather than something to fix.

quote: So Thursday, I'll be busy... we can probably Saturday... Wife's birthday. Could we do, could we do next week?
stewart_read: The customer cycles through three different date options in a single breath (Thursday unavailable, Saturday tentative around a birthday, then a request to push to next week entirely) driven by the fact he hasn't moved yet. The rep tracks this accurately and lands on a real date rather than forcing an artificial lock, which is the correct handling of a genuinely fluid schedule rather than an objection to overcome.
alternative_hypothesis: A stricter reading would flag this as the rep losing control of the booking cadence by letting the date shift three times, but the underlying driver (military move timeline) is a real constraint, not resistance, so accommodation was the right call.
coaching_implication: No correction needed on this thread — cite as an example of appropriately reading a hard constraint versus a soft objection.

quote: So, like, whoever's gonna be calling me, is it gonna be the same area code? It's just because, like, I get so much so many, like, random ass phone calls, you know, that I don't answer.
stewart_read: The customer raises, at the very end and unprompted, a real risk to the appointment holding: he screens and ignores unknown numbers, and the specialist will be calling from a number he's never seen. The rep's fix (have the text include the caller's number) is reasonable but is offered only after the customer asked for it, not proactively as part of button-up.
coaching_implication: This should be a standard button-up element on every call, not a reactive fix: tell every customer upfront that the specialist calls from a rotating number and that the reminder text will include it, before the customer has to ask.
